docs.title: The tower that decides who gets in.
docs.text:
An identity provider for the Symfony ecosystem. On the map of a Symfony application the interface is Symfony, the API is API Platform, and the identity provider is always somewhere else. Beffroi paints that last box the same colour as the other two.

Get started What is Beffroi?

docs.title: What it will not do
docs.text:
Secure by default means there is no option to do it wrong: no implicit flow, no password grant, PKCE with S256 only, redirect URIs compared exactly, iss in every authorization response. Those are properties of the code, not settings of a file.

Secure by default

docs.title: The standalone application
docs.text:
beffroi/op is a provider you deploy rather than a provider you assemble: a Symfony skeleton on the bundle, served by FrankenPHP in worker mode, with PostgreSQL for the model and a broker for the writes the protocol does not wait on.

It is the deployment the project supports, and the one the conformance plans are run against, so a profile reported green is green on this application.

docs.title: Why there is one at all
docs.text: The bundle alone leaves a dozen decisions to whoever installs it: the web server, the worker, the broker, the key management client, the migrations, the two planes, the images. Those decisions are the same for almost everybody, so the project makes them once, in an application, instead of writing them again in a guide. A team that wants to make them differently still can: the bundle is the same bundle.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
Page What it covers Deployment The image, FrankenPHP in worker mode, and the two planes Configuration The environment the application reads, and what each variable decides Operating it Rotating keys, rewrapping data keys, migrations, backups Observability What the provider records of a request, a session and a token

The repository is beffroi-auth/op. It lives inside a working copy of the monorepo during development, and is published on its own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Everything that varies by deployment is an environment variable: the issuer, the key management DSN, the database, the broker, the lifetimes, the host that asks for a client certificate. Nothing secret is in a file that is committed.

This page will list the variables and what each one decides.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The application runs on FrankenPHP in worker mode, with a process per plane when a deployment separates them, PostgreSQL for the model and a broker for the asynchronous writes. TLS terminates in front of it, and the listener that asks for a client certificate is a host of its own.

The security headers are shared by a rule: the bundle writes what belongs to a page it builds, the application writes what belongs to a deployment, and neither writes a header the other does, because a header written twice collides rather than being replaced. What this application answers with is in two files of its configuration, and nothing it writes is written again in the web server or at the edge.

The headers

This page will describe the image, the processes, the health checks, and the reverse proxy.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Every session and every event carries a request context: address, user agent, and what is derived from them, enriched asynchronously so that a sign-in never waits on it. What is recorded, and for how long, is a property of the deployment.

The acts of the provider are written down, kept and read: who did what, when and from where. Nothing turns the journal on; what a deployment configures is how long an act is kept, six months by default, which is the duration the CNIL deliberation 2021-122 holds for a log of connections. A deployment under another obligation says its own, and a timed step forgets what is past it.

  • Every act done in the name of a person names them, by the subject their account carries, and the client it was done on behalf of. That is what lets a person read what happened to their account, on the page of their acts, and what beffroi:user:journal reads to answer a request about it.
  • The reads that hand a person over to a third party are acts too: an introspection that tells a resource server who a token names, and a UserInfo answer.
  • What a client was given is kept beside the act that gave it: at each issue of tokens, the scopes, the claims asked for by name and the authorization details, sealed, and the shape of the token, so that what an application obtained of somebody still has an answer after the consent it was given under was taken back.
  • What a record used to say is kept the same way, under a retention of its own, history.retention, six months as well unless the deployment says otherwise.

What a client was given is kept exactly as long as the act that gave it, and forgotten by the same timed step: an act whose details are gone, or details whose act is gone, would be half an answer.

A provenance says from where and not only from which address. The enrichment reads the GeoLite2 databases of addresses, refreshed weekly by a timed step and installed by beffroi:geoip:refresh. They are published by MaxMind under their own licence, so nothing is shipped and nothing is downloaded without a licence key: a deployment that names none serves every flow with a provenance that says an address and no place.

This page will describe the logs, the metrics, the audit records, and the retention.

docs.title: Operating it
docs.text:
A provider is operated, not installed once: keys rotate, data keys are rewrapped, migrations run, backups are taken and restored. Each of those has a command, and each command says what it did.

Some of it is not operated at all, because time does it: one timed step per thing that comes round, each one handled like any other write, so a deployment that runs the worker runs them.

Every What it does minute Advances the lifecycle of the keys: stages a successor for a key that has worked its age, activates a staged key whose delay has elapsed, retires a key past its date hour Drops the clients nobody uses any more, forgets the archives past their week, drops the rows that can no longer do anything, and reads again the metadata of the SAML service providers and upstream identity providers day Forgets the acts of the journal past their retention, and the changes of a record past theirs week Refreshes the databases of addresses, which is the cadence they are published at

beffroi:doctor is what to ask first when something does not work: it reads, writes nothing, and says which points this deployment answers for.

This page will describe the routine operations, and the two that are not routine: a compromised key, and a restore.
